newsitem.title: USA: Clinton threatens veto of comp time bill.
newsitem.headline: Clinton threatens veto of comp time bill.

text.p: President Clinton threatened Wednesday to veto a bill that would let private employees take time off instead of extra pay, saying it endangers fair labor standards.

"I strongly oppose House Resolution 1 (the Working Families Flexibility Act) and will veto this bill if passed in its current form," Clinton said in a letter to House Speaker Newt Gingrich, Republican of Georgia.

"Although I am prepared to support and sign a responsible comp time bill, I intend to veto any legislation that fails to guarantee real choice for employees, real protection against employer abuse, and preservation of fair labor standards such as the 40-hour work week and the right to overtime pay," Clinton said in the letter to Gingrich.

The president said he would support an amendment offered by Rep. George Miller, a California Democrat, arguing that it would allow comp time without endangering fair labor standards and without burdening business with greater costs or risks.

"We should enact comp time legislation this year that meets the needs of working families and U.S. businesses," Clinton said. He said he favored employee-choice flex-time and expansion of the law so workers could take leave for parent-teacher conferences or doctor visits.
